title: Taxation basics: equity vs debt, STCG and LTCG
objectives: Explain how equity and debt fund gains are taxed in broad terms.
Work out a simple long-term capital gains tax example.
Know when to send a client to a tax adviser.
body_md:
<!-- TODO-VERIFY: every rate and threshold on this page changes with the Finance Act. Check the current rates before each training cycle and before quoting them to a client. -->

Tax depends on the fund's **type** and how long the client **holds** the units. A distributor explains the basics and sends the client to a tax adviser for personal advice.

| Fund type | Short-term gain | Long-term gain |
|---|---|---|
| Equity-oriented (at least 65% in Indian equity) | Held up to 12 months: taxed at 20% | Held over 12 months: 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh in a year |
| Specified debt funds (bought on or after 1 April 2023) | Taxed at the client's slab rate, regardless of holding period | Same as short-term |
| Other hybrid and debt funds | Rules depend on the equity share and holding period | Check the current rules |

Figures are as understood at the time of writing. Add 4% health and education cess, and surcharge where it applies.

## Points that surprise clients

- **A switch or redemption is a sale** and can trigger tax, even within the same fund house.
- **Dividends (IDCW)** are taxed at the client's slab rate, and a TDS may apply.
- **NRIs** face TDS on redemption at the applicable rate, so the amount received is lower than the redemption value.
- **Set-off:** losses can offset gains under the rules, and some can be carried forward.

> **Investor takeaway:** Check tax before every switch or redemption. Ask your tax adviser about your own position.
example: A client sells equity fund units held for 3 years with a gain of ₹3,00,000. The first ₹1,25,000 of long-term gains in the year is exempt, so ₹1,75,000 is taxed at 12.5% = ₹21,875, plus 4% cess of ₹875, about ₹22,750 in total.
say: Tax depends on the fund type and how long you hold. Let's check before we sell.
For your own tax position, please confirm with your tax adviser.
never: This switch has no tax because it is the same fund house.

check.q: A client moves money between two schemes of the same AMC. For tax, this is treated as:
o: A redemption plus a purchase, which can be taxable
check.why: A switch is a sale and a purchase, so it can trigger tax and exit load.

check.q: For an equity fund, which holding period generally separates short-term from long-term gains?
check.why: For equity-oriented funds, the dividing line is 12 months.

check.q: Who should you refer a client to for advice on their personal tax position?
o: A tax adviser or chartered accountant
check.why: A distributor explains basics and refers personal tax questions to a qualified adviser.
